description: The bar chart, titled “Evaluation Based on Different Tasks,” visually compares the accuracy of three model variants—“Base” (orange), “RMU with Enhanced GCG” (light green), and “RMU” (yellow)—across two distinct evaluation tasks: “MCQ Eval” and “Generation Eval.” The vertical y-axis represents “Accuracy,” scaled from 0.0 to 0.6 in increments of 0.2, while the horizontal x-axis categorizes the two tasks. In “MCQ Eval,” the “Base” model achieves an accuracy of 0.644, the “RMU with Enhanced GCG” variant reaches 0.539, and the “RMU” model scores 0.299, indicating that Enhanced GCG partially mitigates the accuracy drop from the base model. In “Generation Eval,” the “Base” model attains 0.597, “RMU with Enhanced GCG” drops to 0.263, and “RMU” falls further to 0.106, revealing a significantly diminished effectiveness of Enhanced GCG in this task. The chart’s legend clearly maps colors to model types, and the stacked arrangement of bars within each task group visually emphasizes the relative performance gaps. The caption underscores that Enhanced GCG’s effectiveness is task-dependent, performing well in generation tasks involving maximum letter probability (as implied by MCQ Eval) but poorly in broader text generation tasks (Generation Eval), supporting the paper’s claim that existing LLM unlearning evaluations are inconclusive due to such variability.
